prompt_text: What are the best online courses for learning shadow work and spiritual practice?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “best” program — the right course depends on whether you want psychologically grounded shadow work (Jungian/therapeutic), trauma-informed somatic healing, or a contemplative spiritual practice (meditation, yoga, mysticism). Below are reputable, well-rated online options in each category, with why they’re useful and who they’re best for.

Recommended courses & platforms

- Jung Platform (paid)
  - What: Focused online courses and programs taught by Jungian analysts (e.g., James Hollis and others) on shadow work, dreams, archetypes and integration.
  - Why: Grounded in Jungian depth psychology, good for serious study of the shadow with experienced clinicians.
  - Best for: People who want theory + clinical-style guidance and integration.

- Sounds True (paid)
  - What: Publisher of spiritual and psychological courses — hosts classic shadow work programs (Debbie Ford’s work and others), plus mindfulness and integration offerings.
  - Why: Established publisher with high-quality audio/video programs from experienced teachers.
  - Best for: Those who want structured, well-produced programs combining psychology and personal development.

- The Shift Network (paid)
  - What: Online summits and multi-week courses led by experienced spiritual teachers and therapists (shadow integration, trauma healing, awakening).
  - Why: Large selection, some deep multi-week cohorts with community support.
  - Best for: People seeking guided transformational programs and community.

- Udemy / Skillshare (mostly paid, frequent discounts)
  - What: Many introductory courses on “shadow work,” inner child healing, Jungian concepts, and spiritual practices.
  - Why: Affordable, broad selection; quality varies, so read reviews and instructor bios.
  - Best for: Beginners wanting affordable introductions or a-la-carte lessons.

- Insight Timer (free + paid)
  - What: Huge library of free guided meditations and many multi-week courses by teachers like Tara Brach and Jack Kornfield.
  - Why: Accessible, good for building daily contemplative practice and finding wise teachers.
  - Best for: People who want meditation, mindfulness, and short courses to support inner work.

- Palouse Mindfulness / MBSR online (free or low-cost)
  - What: Full Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) course modeled on Jon Kabat‑Zinn’s program (Palouse is free; there are many paid certified MBSR online courses as well).
  - Why: Evidence-based, trauma-informed mindfulness training that supports regulation and presence — a good foundation before deep shadow work.
  - Best for: Anyone wanting an evidence-based meditation practice to stabilize emotional reactivity.

- Isha Foundation — Inner Engineering (paid)
  - What: Online course teaching a structured meditation, kriya and daily practice (Sukshma Kriya / Shambhavi).
  - Why: Well-organized practice package for building sustained spiritual routine.
  - Best for: People seeking a practical daily spiritual technology (yoga/meditation).

- Traction toward somatic/trauma-informed training (various providers)
  - Examples: TRE (David Berceli), workshops on polyvagal theory and somatic approaches (NICABM, Pete Walker’s resources), or intro workshops from somatic-experiencing practitioners.
  - Why: Shadow work often uncovers trauma; somatic training helps regulate the nervous system and avert retraumatization.
  - Best for: Those with a trauma history or strong somatic reactivity.

Safety & selection tips (important)
- If you have a significant trauma history, severe depression, suicidality, or psychosis, do shadow work only with a trauma‑informed mental health professional. Online courses can stir strong material.
- Look for teachers with relevant clinical or long-term training (therapists, Jungian analysts, experienced meditation teachers).
- Prefer offerings that include: guided practices, reflective exercises, integration suggestions, and community or teacher access for questions.
- Read reviews, sample free material or recordings, and choose a course length/responsiveness you can commit to (deep shadow work usually requires weeks‑to‑months).
- Pair shadow work with somatic and mindfulness practices to regulate affect (breathwork, yoga, MBSR-style meditation).

Books & free resources to prepare or supplement
- Meeting the Shadow (edited by Connie Zweig & Jeremiah Abrams) — anthology on shadow work.
- Owning Your Own Shadow (Robert A. Johnson) — concise Jungian primer.
- The Dark Side of the Light Chasers (Debbie Ford) — practical exercises for shadow integration (used widely; do it with caution if you’re sensitive).
- Tara Brach and Jack Kornfield — free talks and meditations on their sites and Insight Timer.
- Palouse Mindfulness (free MBSR-style course).

If you want, tell me:
- whether you prefer psychologically grounded vs spiritual vs somatic approaches,
- your experience level (beginner/intermediate/advanced),
- any mental health history (so I can flag cautions),
and I’ll recommend 2–3 specific courses that match you.
